description: Determine whether a word's abbreviation identifies only that word in a dictionary. An abbreviation keeps the first and last letters and replaces the middle with its length. Example 1: in [deer, door, cake, card], cart is unique because its abbreviation is not used by any dictionary word. Example 2: dear is not unique because it shares an abbreviation with deer and door. Constraints: words contain lowercase letters, and duplicate dictionary entries do not create a different word.
intuition: Uniqueness depends only on the set of distinct dictionary words sharing one abbreviation.

brute_force.approach: For each query, abbreviate every dictionary entry and compare it with the query abbreviation.

optimal.approach: Precompute abbreviation-to-word sets and check whether the set is empty or contains only the queried word.

edge_cases: Words of length one or two abbreviate to themselves.
Repeated copies of the queried word still count as one distinct word.
